mainTopic: What רב חסדא asked about נחמיה, and whether a wall of people may be set up on שבת (the third versus fourth סוכה wall)
overview: Earlier, נחמיה was so absorbed in learning that he walked past his תחום שבת, and רב נחמן ruled: 'Make a wall of people for him and let him come back in.' The גמרא first asks what רב חסדא was unsure about. It proves he was not asking about רבן גמליאל's rule, because רב already ruled on that, so he must have been asking about רבי אליעזר's rule that someone two אמות outside may come back in. Next, רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges רבא with a ברייתא that forbids standing a person in place of a fallen סוכה wall on שבת or יום טוב. רבא answers with another ברייתא that allows using a friend as a wall, so the two ברייתות contradict each other. The גמרא first says they follow רבי אליעזר and the חכמים, but רבי יוחנן says everyone forbids starting a temporary tent. It then tries רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, but that fails as well, because רבי מאיר spoke only about an animal and could not permit a new wall whichever view of temporary tents he follows. The final answer is that both ברייתות follow the רבנן: making the third wall of a סוכה is forbidden, and making the extra fourth wall is permitted. The wording 'its wall fell' proves this.

steps.title: What exactly was רב חסדא unsure about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes laying out two ways to understand רב חסדא's question: was it about רבן גמליאל, or about רבי אליעזר?
steps.simpleTranslation: ...or is the הלכה not like רבן גמליאל? Or perhaps we are dealing with a case where there were not enough people to fill the whole space, and his question was: is the הלכה like רבי אליעזר, or is the הלכה not like רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its question about what רב חסדא was really asking. It offers a second possibility: maybe there weren't enough people to make a wall all the way to the תחום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: people filled the whole distance, so the only question is whether רבן גמליאל's 'closed area' idea is the הלכה. Option two: the human wall stopped short, so נחמיה still had to walk a little bit on his own. Then the question is whether רבי אליעזר's rule, that someone two אמות outside may come back, is the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The words 'or is the הלכה not like רבן גמליאל' are the end of the first option, which started on the previous daf. They are not a new statement.

phrases.english: or is the halacha not like Rabban Gamliel?
phrases.notes: End of the first option, which began on the previous amud.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא, בִּדְלָא מָלוּ גַּבְרֵי עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Or perhaps we are dealing with a case where people did not fill (the whole space),
phrases.notes: The human wall did not reach all the way to the תחום.

phrases.english: and what he was asking was:
Is the halacha like Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר: someone who went two אמות outside the תחום may come back in.

phrases.english: or is the halacha not like Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא, בִּדְלָא מָלוּ גַּבְרֵי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question that began on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was רב חסדא's doubt about רבן גמליאל's rule (if people filled the whole space) or about רבי אליעזר's rule (if they didn't)?

steps.title: It must be the case where people did not fill the space
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the answer is obvious. If people filled the whole space, there would be nothing to ask, because רב already ruled like רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that we are dealing with a case where people did not fill the space. Because if you thought we were dealing with a case where people did fill it, what would he be asking? Didn't רב say: the הלכה is like רבן גמליאל regarding a pen, a stable, and a boat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. רב already ruled like רבן גמליאל, so רב חסדא could not have been unsure about that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the people filled the whole distance, the case would be like רבן גמליאל's closed-in area. רב already gave a clear ruling there, so a scholar like רב חסדא would not have needed to ask. That means option one doesn't work.

keyTerms.meaning: If it would enter your mind (if you were to think)
A pen, a stable, and a boat (enclosed areas where רבן גמליאל lets one walk throughout)

phrases.english: It is obvious that we are dealing with where people did not fill (the space),
for if you were to think
that we are dealing with where people did fill it,
what would he be asking?
Didn't Rav say:
The halacha is like Rabban Gamliel
regarding a pen, a stable, and a boat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 1 by ruling out the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case must be where people did not fill the space, because רב already settled the רבן גמליאל question.

steps.title: So the question was about רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב חסדא's doubt was whether the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we must be dealing with a case where people did not fill the space, and his question was about רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its answer. רב חסדא was asking about רבי אליעזר's two-אמות rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since option one is ruled out, only option two is left. The human wall brought נחמיה close, but he still had to cross the last bit, up to two אמות, by himself. That only works if we follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's question was about רבי אליעזר's rule: can someone who is two אמות outside the תחום come back in? It was not about רבן גמליאל, since רב already ruled on that.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא וַדַּאי בִּדְלָא מָלוּ גַּבְרֵי עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Rather, certainly we are dealing with where people did not fill (the space),
and it was about Rabbi Eliezer's view that he was asking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא וַדַּאי בִּדְלָא מָלוּ גַּבְרֵי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the reasoning in Step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא's doubt was whether the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Support from רב נחמן's word 'let him enter'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב נחמן's wording supports this reading. 'Let him enter' suggests he walks the last part without a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also precise from the wording, since he told him 'let him enter.' What does 'let him enter' mean? Doesn't it mean without a wall?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings extra support from the exact words רב נחמן used in his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן did not just say 'make a wall.' He added 'let him enter.' That extra phrase hints that after the human wall ends, נחמיה walks the last stretch on his own, with no wall. This fits the רבי אליעזר reading.

keyTerms.meaning: This is also precise (the wording supports it)

phrases.english: This is also precise (from the wording),
for he said to him, 'Let him enter.'
What does 'let him enter' mean?
Doesn't it mean without a wall?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from the text for the conclusion in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that רב חסדא's question was about רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's extra word 'יִכָּנֵס', meaning he crosses the final stretch without a wall.

steps.title: Challenge from a fallen סוכה wall
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges רבא with a ברייתא. It says you may not use people to replace a fallen סוכה wall on יום טוב or שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenged רבא: If the wall of a סוכה fell, a person may not stand a person, an animal, or utensils there. He also may not stand a bed upright to spread a sheet over it. This is because one may not make a temporary tent for the first time on יום טוב, and there is no need to say that it is forbidden on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge opens. The ברייתא seems to say you may not make a wall out of people on שבת, which goes against רבא's view that a human wall is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists a person among the things you may not use to make a wall for the סוכה. The reason it gives is that you may not set up a temporary אוהל from scratch on יום טוב, and all the more so on שבת. If a human wall is forbidden there, how could people make a wall for נחמיה on שבת? The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start (newly made, not added to an existing one)
Needless to say (all the more so)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about a סוכה, not about תחומין. The challenge works only by comparison: if people can't serve as a wall for a סוכה on שבת, maybe they can't serve as a wall for anything else on שבת either.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenges the whole idea that a human wall may be made on שבת. Everything said about נחמיה depends on that idea.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak challenged Rava:
If its (the sukkah's) wall fell,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַעֲמִיד בָּהּ אָדָם בְּהֵמָה וְכֵלִים.
phrases.english: one may not stand a person, an animal, or utensils there.
And he may not stand the bed upright
to spread a sheet over it,
because one may not make a temporary tent
for the first time on Yom Tov,
and needless to say on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from defining רב חסדא's question and attacks the basic idea that a human wall may be made on שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's position that a wall of people may be set up on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids standing a person in place of a fallen סוכה wall on יום טוב, and all the more so on שבת, because it counts as making a new temporary אוהל. That seems to forbid human walls on שבת.

steps.title: רבא answers with a source that permits it
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the challenge with a different ברייתא. It allows a person to stand as a wall so his friend can eat, drink, and sleep in the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You are quoting a source to me, and I am quoting a source to you. 'A person may use his friend as a wall so that he can eat, drink, and sleep in the סוכה. He may also stand a bed upright and spread a sheet over it so the sun does not beat down on a dead body or on food.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not give up. He brings his own ברייתא, which says you may use a person as a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא said people may not replace a fallen סוכה wall on שבת or יום טוב. רבא's ברייתא says you may use your friend as a wall. So רבא has a source that supports his ruling. The bed-and-sheet case is a second example of making a quick, temporary cover.

keyTerms.meaning: A person may use his friend as a wall
A wall, here the wall of a סוכה
He may stand the bed upright

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ לִי מֵהָא,
phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: You tell me from this source,
and I tell you from this source:
phrases.notes: רבא sets his source against the other one.

phrases.english: A person may make his friend into a wall
so that he may eat, drink, and sleep (in the סוכה).
And he may stand the bed upright
and spread a sheet over it
so that the sun will not beat down
on the dead body or on the food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ לִי מֵהָא, וַאֲנָא אָמֵינָא לָךְ מֵהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן בר יצחק's ברייתא with an opposing ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that people may be used as a wall
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: עושה אדם את חבירו דופן

steps.title: The two sources contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the two ברייתות now contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: These two ברייתות contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that one ברייתא forbids using a person as a wall and the other permits it. This line sets up the search for an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is no longer about רבא. Now there are two sources that disagree, and the גמרא must explain how both can be true.

phrases.english: They contradict one another!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the two ברייתות side by side and notes the clash.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about using a person as a wall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא forbids and the other permits the same act.

steps.title: First answer: the window shutter dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says one ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר and the other follows רבנן. It proves this from their argument about a window shutter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, and that ברייתא follows רבנן. As the משנה teaches about a window shutter: רבי אליעזר says that if it is tied on and hanging, you may close the window with it, and if not, you may not. The חכמים say that either way you may close the window with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר is strict about making even a temporary wall on שבת, so he matches the ברייתא that forbids. The חכמים allow a loose shutter, so they match the ברייתא that permits using a person as a wall.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; this is the start of an answer

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one follows Rabbi Eliezer, that one follows the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: פְּקַק הַחַלּוֹן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as we learned: A window shutter. Rabbi Eliezer says:
When it is tied and hanging, one may close (the window) with it,
and if not, one may not close with it.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ פּוֹקְקִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: And the Sages say: Either way, one may close with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הָא — רַבָּנַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seem to follow one view and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidding ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר. The permitting ברייתא follows the חכמים.

steps.title: Everyone forbids starting a temporary tent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first answer. רבי יוחנן said everyone agrees you may not start a temporary tent. The argument is only about adding to one that already exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was said about this argument: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees that you may not start making a temporary tent on יום טוב, and certainly not on שבת. They only argue about adding to one. רבי אליעזר says you may not add on יום טוב, and certainly not on שבת. The חכמים say you may add even on שבת, and certainly on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first answer by quoting רבי יוחנן's explanation of the window shutter argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The window shutter argument is only about adding to a structure that already stands. Even the חכמים forbid making a temporary tent from scratch. So the permitting ברייתא cannot simply be the חכמים, and the contradiction comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said about it (a later אמורא's explanation)
To add on (to an existing structure)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up starting a tent with adding to one. Everyone forbids starting one. The argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים is only about adding.

phrases.english: But it was stated about it:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין אֹהֶל עֲרַאי
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that one may not make a temporary tent
from the start on a Festival,
and needless to say on Shabbat.
They argued only about adding,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵין מוֹסִיפִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: for Rabbi Eliezer says: One may not add on a Festival,
and needless to say on Shabbat.
And the Sages say: One may add on Shabbat,
and needless to say on a Festival!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the permitting ברייתא follows the חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים only permit adding. Using a person as a wall is building from scratch, which everyone forbids.

steps.title: Second answer: is an animal a valid wall?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. The two ברייתות follow רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, who argue about whether an animal can be a סוכה wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult. This ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, and that one follows רבי יהודה. As a ברייתא teaches: If someone made an animal into a סוכה wall, רבי מאיר says it is not valid, and רבי יהודה says it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first answer fell, the גמרא answers the contradiction a new way, using a different argument between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says a living wall is not a real wall, so placing a person there is not building, and it is allowed. רבי יהודה says a living wall is a real wall, so placing a person there counts as building a wall, and it is forbidden. So the permitting ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, and the forbidding ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but רבי מאיר, who says the wall is not valid, is the one who permits it on שבת. If it is not a real wall, putting it up is not building.
steps.whatToRemember: This answer ties the contradiction to the argument over a living wall. If it counts as a real wall (רבי יהודה), setting it up is forbidden. If it does not (רבי מאיר), it is allowed. Steps 12-15 reject this answer, and step 16 gives the final one.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא — כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָא — כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: this one follows Rabbi Meir, that one follows Rabbi Yehuda.
As it was taught: If he made an animal a wall for the sukka,
Rabbi Meir rules it unfit,
and Rabbi Yehuda rules it fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָא — כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer from step 8 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא (new pair)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות follow רבי אליעזר and the חכמים, but that answer was rejected.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות follow רבי מאיר (a living wall is not a wall, so it is permitted) and רבי יהודה (a living wall is a wall, so it is forbidden).

steps.title: How each opinion fits one of the two ברייתות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out its new answer. רבי מאיר holds that a living creature is not a real wall, so on שבת standing as a wall is permitted. רבי יהודה holds that it is a real wall, so on שבת it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר disqualifies such a wall there, by סוכה. This shows he holds it is not a real wall. So here, on שבת, he permits it, because the person is not really doing anything. רבי יהודה accepts such a wall there, by סוכה. This shows he holds it is a real wall. So here, on שבת, he forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the answer from step 10. It shows exactly how רבי מאיר matches the lenient ברייתא and רבי יהודה matches the strict ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is simple. If a living wall does not count as a real מחיצה, then standing as one on שבת is not 'building' anything, so it is allowed. If it does count as a real מחיצה, then making one on שבת is like building a temporary structure, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: disqualifies, says it does not work
this shows that, so we see that

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the direction. The one who is STRICT by סוכה (רבי מאיר says the wall is invalid) is LENIENT on שבת, because if it is not a wall, you built nothing. The one who is lenient by סוכה is strict on שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir, who disqualifies there (by sukka) —
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of an animal used as a sukka wall.

phrases.english: so we see that it is not a wall;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא שָׁרֵי, דְּלָאו מִידֵּי קָא עָבֵיד.
phrases.english: here (on Shabbat) he permits, because he is not doing anything.
phrases.notes: Standing there is not considered building.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, who validates there —
so we see that it is a wall; here he forbids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the mechanism of the answer given in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות contradict each other with no explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ברייתא follows רבי מאיר (a living wall is not a real wall). The strict ברייתא follows רבי יהודה (it is a real wall).

steps.title: רבי מאיר only spoke about an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. We only heard רבי מאיר disqualify an animal as a wall. Did we ever hear him disqualify a person or utensils?
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really think so? Say that you heard רבי מאיר disqualify an animal. Did you hear him say the same about a person and utensils?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from steps 10 and 11. It says the comparison to רבי מאיר does not fit the case of a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's reason for rejecting an animal may be special to animals, for example that it might walk away. A person stays where he decides to stay, and utensils do not move on their own. So רבי מאיר may agree that a person is a real wall. If so, we cannot use him to explain the ברייתא that permits a person to stand as a wall, since that ברייתא also mentions people and utensils.

keyTerms.meaning: and can you really think so? (opens an objection)

phrases.english: And can you really think so?
phrases.notes: A standard opening for rejecting what was just said.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּהֵמָה.
phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Meir rule this about an animal.
Did you hear him rule this about a person and utensils?
phrases.notes: A person and utensils do not wander off like an animal might.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from steps 10 and 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר holds a living creature is not a real wall in general.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר only spoke about an animal, probably for an animal-specific reason. You cannot stretch his ruling to a person or utensils, which the ברייתא also includes.

steps.title: Whose view would רבי מאיר follow about a temporary tent?
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: if רבי מאיר follows his teacher רבי אליעזר, then even adding to a temporary tent on שבת is forbidden. So how could רבי מאיר permit making a wall out of a person?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: whose opinion does רבי מאיר follow? If he follows רבי אליעזר, then רבי אליעזר forbids even adding to a temporary tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another problem with the answer. It asks which earlier view רבי מאיר holds about temporary tents on שבת, and starts with the option of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes back to the window-shutter argument (steps 8-9). רבי אליעזר forbids even ADDING to a temporary tent on שבת. If רבי מאיר follows him, then making a whole new wall from a person should surely be forbidden, which contradicts the lenient ruling we gave רבי מאיר. Steps 14-15 check the other option, that he follows the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: to add (to an existing temporary tent)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an answer has to fit every part of the סוגיא. Assigning a view to רבי מאיר must also match the rules about temporary tents that the גמרא already set up.

phrases.english: And furthermore — according to whom does Rabbi Meir hold?
If according to Rabbi Eliezer —
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר is רבי מאיר's teacher.

phrases.english: he forbids even adding.
phrases.notes: From the window-shutter argument: even adding to a temporary tent is forbidden, so making a new one surely is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the same answer, independent of the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר permits making a person into a wall on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי מאיר follows רבי אליעזר, who forbids even adding to a temporary tent, then he should surely forbid starting a new wall. That contradicts the lenient ruling given to him.

steps.title: Or does רבי מאיר follow the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues its second challenge. If רבי מאיר does not follow רבי אליעזר, then he must follow the רבנן. The next step shows why that option fails too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say that רבי מאיר holds according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other option in its question 'whose view does רבי מאיר follow?': maybe he follows the רבנן, who argue with רבי אליעזר. This line sets up the next step, which shows this option fails too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed that if רבי מאיר follows his teacher רבי אליעזר, he could not permit a new wall, since רבי אליעזר forbids even adding to a temporary tent. So the only other choice is that רבי מאיר follows the רבנן, who are lenient about adding. Step 15 tests whether that leniency is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages, the majority view, here the ones who argue with רבי אליעזר

phrases.english: Rather, according to the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: The second option: רבי מאיר follows the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the dilemma opened in step 13 about whose view רבי מאיר follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second side of a dilemma about רבי מאיר's underlying view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר might follow רבי אליעזר about temporary tents.
steps.terutzMaskana: The other option is that רבי מאיר follows the רבנן, who are lenient about adding to a temporary tent. Step 15 shows this does not help.

steps.title: The רבנן only allowed adding, not starting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes off the second option for רבי מאיר. The רבנן only allowed adding to an existing temporary tent. They never allowed making one from scratch, so the רבי מאיר answer fails either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that the רבנן said it is permitted to add. Did they ever say it is permitted to make one from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion. The רבנן only allowed adding to a tent, and that does not cover building a new wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes back to רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 9: everyone agrees you may not start a temporary tent on שבת, and the argument is only about adding to one. So whether רבי מאיר follows רבי אליעזר or the רבנן, he could not permit putting up a new wall. The רבי מאיר / רבי יהודה answer falls, and step 16 gives a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: to add on to something that already exists
from the start, for the first time
was it ever said? (a challenge question)

steps.confusionAlert: Here לכתחילה does not mean 'ideally, before the fact,' as it often does. It means making something from scratch, as opposed to adding to something already there.

phrases.english: Say that the Rabbis said it is permitted to add;
but to make it from the start, did they say that?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: no, they never said that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן לְהוֹסִיף, לְכַתְּחִילָּה מִי אֲמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the second option of the dilemma (step 14) also fails, which completes the attack on the רבי מאיר answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר, if he follows the רבנן, permits making a person into a wall on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if רבי מאיר follows the רבנן, they only permit adding to an existing temporary tent. Putting up a new wall is starting one, which everyone forbids, as רבי יוחנן said. So רבי מאיר cannot be the source of the permitting ברייתא either way.

steps.title: Both follow the רבנן: third wall versus fourth wall
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: both ברייתות follow the רבנן. Utensils may not be used for the third wall, which makes the סוכה kosher. They may be used for the fourth wall, which is extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both this ברייתא and that one follow the רבנן. The contradiction between utensils and utensils is not difficult. This one is talking about the third wall, and that one is talking about the fourth wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. There is no argument between the ברייתות, because they are talking about two different walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה is kosher once it has its third wall, so setting up that wall on שבת counts as starting a tent and is forbidden. The fourth wall adds nothing to the סוכה's kosher status, so it is just an extra add-on and is permitted. The contradiction is solved by telling apart two cases, not by assigning the ברייתות to different תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: this one and that one, meaning both sources
it is not difficult, there is no real contradiction
the third wall, the one that makes the סוכה kosher
the fourth wall, which is extra and not required

steps.whatToRemember: Utensils as a wall on שבת: forbidden for the third wall, because it makes the סוכה kosher and so counts as making something new. Permitted for the fourth wall, because it is extra. Both rulings follow the רבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea in הלכות שבת: whether an act counts as 'making' depends on whether it creates something with real legal meaning.

phrases.english: Rather: this one and that one both follow the Rabbis.
And the contradiction of utensils against utensils is not difficult:
this one is about the third wall,
phrases.notes: Forbidden, because the third wall makes the סוכה kosher.

phrases.english: that one is about the fourth wall.
phrases.notes: Permitted, because the fourth wall is extra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed attempts to assign the ברייתות to different תנאים with a distinction between cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling apart two cases (third wall versus fourth wall)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות argue, so they must follow different תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow the רבנן. One is about the third wall, which is forbidden, and the other is about the fourth wall, which is permitted.

steps.title: The wording 'its wall fell' supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: The wording of the forbidding ברייתא, 'its wall fell,' points to a needed wall. That supports the third-wall reading. The גמרא concludes: learn from this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, because it teaches: 'its wall fell.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by pointing to the exact wording of the ברייתא, and then declares the answer proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Its wall fell' suggests the סוכה lost an important wall that it needs in order to be kosher. That fits the third wall, where setting up a wall of utensils is forbidden. The other ברייתא just speaks of a wall in general, which fits the extra fourth wall.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is also precise and supports this
learn from this, it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: The final resolution is proven from the wording: the third wall is forbidden and the fourth wall is permitted, and both rulings follow the רבנן.

phrases.english: It is also precise, since it teaches:
'its wall fell.'
phrases.notes: This points to a wall the סוכה needs, meaning the third wall.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the Step 16 answer from the text itself.
steps.raayaObject: The third wall versus fourth wall distinction
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'נפל דופנה' in the forbidding ברייתא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both ברייתות follow the רבנן. Using utensils for the third wall is forbidden, and using them for the fourth wall is permitted.
